<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 41 · Example 6.10</p>

::: notes


The booklet attributes this to “Advanced HSC – Bank Question” without a year or question number. Do not invent an examination reference. The graph is redrawn as exact vector points with the original t_n label and six values equal to 1. On-screen choices 1–4 correspond to booklet A–D. Correct 4 (D): constant sequence 1,1,… has r=1. It is also arithmetic, but d=0, not 1. Its nth partial sum is n, so choices 1 and 3 do not describe its total. No limiting-sum formula is needed. Six observed points do not uniquely determine the continuation; the prompt correctly says “could be”. Use the normal simultaneous finger routine. Ready: explain why being both AP and GP does not make choice 2 correct. Divided: compare consecutive differences and ratios. Reteach: list S_1=1, S_2=2, S_3=3. Reset hides correctness. This untimed review is separate from the timed hinge.

:::
